metaDescription: Six electric window vacuums compared on blade width, battery life, tank size and extension poles, with streak-free tips for glass and shower doors.
expertTake: The Karcher WV 6 Plus is the best pick because its 280 mm nozzle, quoted 100 minute battery life and replaceable suction lip keep it working through a whole house of windows. The Karcher WV 1 Plus is the value choice for showers and mirrors at about 1.1 pounds. Anyone with textured, etched or rough glass should skip these tools, because a flat squeegee blade needs a smooth surface.
introParagraphs: An electric window vacuum sprays or wipes cleaner onto glass, then pulls the dirty water into a small tank with a silicone blade and a suction slot. It prevents the drips that run down a wet window and finish as streaks, which is the main complaint with a hand squeegee.

The machine is a finishing tool, not a cleaner. Dirt must be loosened first, the blade must be flat and the glass must be smooth. This guide compares six models on blade width, battery life, tank size and reach, and it explains the technique that makes any of them leave a clean surface.

products.name: Karcher WV 6 Plus battery window vacuum with 280 mm nozzle and extra-long battery run
products.description:
Karcher builds the WV 6 Plus for whole-house window work. A 280 millimeter wide nozzle absorbs water and dissolved dirt, and the listing quotes up to 100 minutes of battery life and up to 300 square meters of cleaned surface per charge. That endurance is the longest in this guide, so it suits a home with many panes.

Innovative suction and lip technology aims for drip- and streak-free results on windows, tiles and mirrors. An LED charge indicator shows the battery state, and a replaceable suction lip means a nicked blade does not retire the tool. The blade is the part that wears out, so a replaceable one is a real long-term advantage. A tool whose blade cannot be swapped is a short-term purchase, however good the motor.

Compared with the WV 2 and WV 1 Plus, the nozzle is wider and the battery lasts much longer. A wider blade covers more glass per pass and is harder to use on small panes. Empty and dry the tank after use to avoid a musty smell. Best suited to homes with large windows and sliding doors.
products.bestFor: Homes with many large windows and sliding doors that need a long battery life.
pros: 280 mm nozzle covers large panes quickly
Up to 100 minutes of battery life
cons: Wide blade is awkward on small panes
Runs pricier than the compact models
Tank needs emptying on large jobs

products.name: Karcher WV 2 Universal cordless window vacuum with 360 degree comfort clean

specList.label: Angle
specList.value: 360 degree Comfort Clean, works sideways or upside down

specList.label: Surfaces
specList.value: Windows, mirrors, glass shower doors and smooth tiles

products.description:
The WV 2 Universal is Karcher's all-rounder. The 360 degree Comfort Clean technology lets you work sideways or even upside down, so ceilings of glass and low panes are reachable. A built-in electric vacuum pulls dirty water away from the glass instantly, leaving a streak-free finish in one pass.

It goes beyond windows, with the maker listing mirrors, glass shower doors and other smooth surfaces. That makes it a tool for bathrooms as much as for windows. The ability to work at any angle matters on a shower door or an overhead skylight, where a gravity-fed tank would fail.

Compared with the WV 6 Plus, it has a smaller footprint and less battery life. Compared with the WV 1 Plus, it adds angle freedom and a more general focus. Wipe the blade clean after use, and empty the tank before storing. It suits households that want one tool for windows, mirrors and shower glass.
products.bestFor: Households that want one tool for windows, mirrors and shower doors at any angle.

Cleans windows, mirrors and shower glass

products.name: Karcher WV 1 Plus electric window vacuum with 10 inch squeegee, 1.1 lb

specList.label: Speed claim
specList.value: 3 times faster than a hand squeegee

products.description:
The WV 1 Plus is the light, compact Karcher. A 10 inch electric squeegee sits in the hand at only 1.1 pounds, which makes it easy to carry through a bathroom and use overhead. The maker claims it cleans three times faster than a manual approach on windows, showers and mirrors.

The workflow is spray, wipe and vacuum away the grime. Keeping surfaces generously wet while cleaning and wiping the edges helps the blade glide. For textured tile, the maker suggests extra steps to prepare the surface, which shows the tool's limits.

Compared with the WV 6 Plus, it has a narrower blade and shorter run time. It suits small windows, shower doors and mirrors rather than whole-house jobs. Empty the tank after use and wipe the blade. It is the value pick for bathrooms and small panes.
products.bestFor: Showers, mirrors and small windows where a light hand-held tool is easiest.
pros: Claimed three times faster than a hand squeegee
cons: Narrow blade is slow on large windows
Shorter run time than the WV 6 Plus

specList.label: Reach

specList.label: Kit

products.description:
This cordless window vacuum adds a 30 to 40 inch extension pole to an 11 inch blade, which is how you reach high windows without a ladder. The listing describes it as suitable for windows, mirrors, shower doors, tiles and other compatible smooth surfaces. A 2000Pa suction rating collects dirty water directly into the tank.

The pole is the point, since reach is the problem with window cleaning. An extension adds wobble, so a steady hand matters at the far end. The suction rating is a marketing figure, as there is no common test, so judge the tool by blade quality and flatness instead.

Compared with the Karcher WV 1 Plus, it adds reach and loses the established brand and parts supply. Wipe the blade and check it for nicks, because a damaged edge leaves streaks. It suits homes with high or hard-to-reach windows.
products.bestFor: Homes with high or awkward windows where a ladder is a hazard.

Kit covers windows, mirrors and tile
cons: Suction figure is a marketing number

products.name: Cordless electric window vacuum squeegee with 2000Pa, 11 inch blade and 150 mL tank
products.description:
This white cordless window vacuum pairs an 11 inch blade with a 150 mL transparent tank. The built-in 2200mAh rechargeable battery gives cordless freedom, and a 2000Pa suction rating lifts dirty water and cleaning solution. The clear tank is detachable and easy to rinse.

A 150 mL tank fills quickly on a big window, so frequent emptying is normal. A transparent tank lets you see how full it is. The blade is wider than the WV 1 Plus and narrower than the WV 6 Plus.

Compared with the extension-pole model, it has no pole and costs less. It suits apartments and bathrooms rather than tall windows. Rinse the tank and dry the blade after use. It is the budget pick for general glass cleaning.
products.bestFor: Apartments and bathrooms where a budget tool with a clear tank is enough.
cons: Suction figure is a marketing number

products.name: ZRHI cordless window vacuum squeegee with 2000Pa suction, 2200mAh battery and 150 ml tank
products.description:
ZRHI offers a cordless window vacuum with a 2000Pa suction rating, a 2200mAh battery and a 150 ml water collection tank. It is a standard design in the budget class, with a silicone blade and a small tank. The listing is brief and does not describe accessories in the data used here.

The specifications match the other budget models in this guide, so the choice rests on price and brand support. A 150 ml tank means frequent emptying, and a marketing suction figure says little about performance. Blade quality is what matters, and listings rarely state it.

Compared with the Karcher models, it lacks a long-standing brand and parts supply. Check the warranty and whether replacement blades are sold. Wipe the blade and empty the tank after use. Best suited to occasional window cleaning at the lowest cost.
products.bestFor: Occasional window and mirror cleaning at the lowest cost.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Blade width runs from the 10 inch WV 1 Plus through 11 inch budget models to the 280 mm WV 6 Plus. A wider blade covers more glass per pass but is awkward on small panes and in shower corners. Flatness matters more than width, because a blade that does not sit flat on the glass leaves streaks. Replaceable lips, as on the WV 6 Plus, extend the tool's life. Run a fingertip along a new blade to feel for burrs, and press the blade flat against the glass before you start. A blade that rocks on the surface will leave a stripe on every pass.

The WV 6 Plus quotes up to 100 minutes and up to 300 square meters per charge, while budget models use 2200mAh cells with typical run times of 25 to 40 minutes. A small home needs less. A home with sliding doors and large panes benefits from a long battery. Charging takes a few hours, usually three to four with a USB-C lead. Plan to charge the tool the night before a big job. A tool that dies halfway through a window leaves a half-wet pane that streaks as it dries.

The budget models list 150 mL tanks, and tank sizes of 100 to 200 mL fill quickly on a large window. Frequent emptying is normal. A transparent tank lets you see the level. Empty and dry the tank after each use to avoid a musty smell.

The extension-pole model adjusts from 30 to 40 inches for high windows, and the WV 2 Universal works sideways or upside down. Poles add wobble and a long tool is harder to control. Choose reach only if you have high windows or skylights. Never lean out of an open window or stand on a rail to reach farther. If a window needs a ladder, a pole and a helper are safer than a stretch.

Listings quote 2000Pa on several budget models. There is no common test standard, so the number is a marketing figure. Judge a tool by blade quality and flatness. Strong suction cannot fix a poor blade. A bright pane of glass shows every line, so check the result from an angle in daylight. Re-wet and repeat a pass instead of dragging a dry blade, which can scratch.

These tools suit smooth glass, mirrors and shower doors. They are not for textured, rough or etched glass. Loosen dirt first with a scrubber pad and keep the surface wet. Work on shaded glass, since sun-baked glass dries before the blade passes. Start at the top of the pane and work down in overlapping strips. Wipe the frame with a dry cloth afterward, because drips along the edge are the last place streaks appear.

howWeEvaluated.title: Class purity
howWeEvaluated.description: We kept only electric window vacuum squeegees. Manual squeegees, robot window cleaners and pressure washers that appeared in related searches were removed. That left six distinct machines.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blade and nozzle
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared blade widths and replaceability. The WV 6 Plus lists 280 mm and a replaceable lip, and the budget models list 11 in. Blade quality weighed above suction claims.

howWeEvaluated.title: Battery and tank
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared quoted battery life and tank sizes. The WV 6 Plus lists up to 100 minutes, and the budget models list 2200mAh and 150 mL. Practical coverage per charge was the measure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Reach and surfaces
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at extension poles and surface lists. The extension model adjusts 30 to 40 in, and the WV 2 works at any angle. Fit to your windows decides the pick.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership signals
howWeEvaluated.description: Owner complaints keep returning to worn blades, small tanks and mold smell from undried tanks as the common problems. Brand support for replacement blades mattered, since the blade is the wear part of the tool. We also noted whether the listing named the surfaces it suits and left out claims about etched or textured glass.

cards.label: Wide blade
cards.text: The WV 6 Plus has a 280 mm nozzle and a long battery. It covers big panes quickly. It is awkward on small panes.

cards.label: Compact
cards.text: The WV 1 Plus and 10 to 11 inch budget models fit showers and small windows. They are light and easy to store. They need more passes on large glass.

howToChoose.note: Pick wide for large glass. Pick compact for bathrooms.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Streak-free results need a flat, undamaged blade, loosened dirt, a shaded surface and a quick wipe of the edges. A replaceable blade keeps results consistent.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The WV 6 Plus has a replaceable lip. The WV 1 Plus and WV 2 are from a brand with parts support.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You clean many windows or want a tool that lasts for years. The WV 6 Plus earns its cost.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clean a few panes a couple of times a year. A budget model covers it.

maintenance.why: Standing dirty water breeds mold and odor. Leave the tank open to dry.
Dirt on the blade leaves streaks. Wipe it with a clean cloth.
A nicked blade leaves lines. Replace the lip when edges chip.
Cells age faster when stored empty. Avoid leaving it fully discharged.
Dried residue blocks suction. Rinse the nozzle and slot.

faq.a: They reduce drip streaks, but a worn blade or dirty glass will still leave lines. Loosen dirt first and keep the blade flat. Replace nicked blades.

faq.q: Can I use a window vacuum on a shower door?
faq.a: Yes, on smooth glass. The WV 2 Universal and WV 1 Plus list shower doors. Textured glass needs extra prep.
The number is a marketing figure with no common test. Blade quality matters more. Judge by results, not pascals.
Use a mild glass cleaner. Strong cleaners with ammonia can degrade seals. Check the maker's guidance.
In shade, not in direct sun. Sun-baked glass dries before the blade passes. Early morning or an overcast day works well.

faq.q: How long do window vacuums last?
faq.a: Expect several years, with blades and batteries as the usual wear points. Replace blades when nicked and avoid storing the tool empty.
